title: JavaScript — Arrays and common array methods

questions.question: filter vs map: you want paid customer objects only. Which is correct?
options: filter with a test on status, which returns a shorter array.
map, then drop undefined later if you remember.

for...in so inherited keys become extra rows.
questions.explanation: filter keeps elements that pass. map always returns the same length.

options: The check succeeds because 0 means found.
indexOf returns true instead of 0.
indexOf throws if x is at the start.

questions.question: slice(2, 4) on [0,1,2,3,4] yields what?
options: [2, 3] — start inclusive, end exclusive.
[2, 3, 4] — both ends inclusive.
[0, 1] — slice takes a length, not an end.
[2, 4] — it picks those two indices only.
questions.explanation: Same convention as Python slicing and substring end indexes.

questions.question: typeof [] is "object". How do you test for an array?
options: typeof value === "array"
value instanceof String
Array.isArray(value)
value === []
questions.explanation: [] === [] is false (different objects). Array.isArray is the right test.

questions.question: push vs concat when you must not mutate the caller’s payments array?
options: push returns a new array; concat mutates.
neither can add elements.
both mutate, so you must copy with JSON first.
concat (or spread) returns a new array; push mutates.
questions.explanation: push changes length in place. concat/[...arr, x] copy.

questions.question: paidTotals should ignore pending rows. Which pipeline matches the notes?
options: map to amounts first, then hope pending is 0.
filter status === "paid", then reduce with initial 0.
reduce without filter so pending amounts still add.
sort by status, then take index 0.
questions.explanation: Filter then sum, or one reduce that adds only paid rows. Seed 0.

options: a RangeError
null
undefined, not an exception.
questions.explanation: Missing indices are undefined. Check length before assuming a row exists.

options: map
filter
push
slice
questions.explanation: push mutates. map, filter, and slice produce new arrays.

options: undefined so the first row becomes the count.
